## AI Safety

- [Introduction to AI Safety, Ethics, and Society](https://www.aisafetybook.com), Dan Hendrycks ([my notes](ai-safety-book.qmd))
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>A broad, accessible framework for thinking about AI risk. It links technical ideas with ethics and policy.</details>

## Linguistics

### Historical linguistics

- *Historical Linguistics: An Introduction*, Lyle Campbell
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>The standard textbook. Clear on sound change, comparative method and reconstruction.</details>
- *Trask's Historical Linguistics*, Robert McColl Millar
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Readable and full of examples. A good companion to Campbell.</details>
- *Linguistic Reconstruction*, Anthony Fox
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Goes deeper into how reconstruction actually works, and what its limits are.</details>

### Indo-European

- *Indo-European Language and Culture: An Introduction*, Benjamin Fortson
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>The go-to overview of Indo-European languages, covering grammar, sound laws and culture together.</details>

## Ancient Languages

### Latin

- *The Regional Diversification of Latin 200 BC – AD 600*, J. N. Adams
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Shows how Latin varied across the Empire. Dense but a real eye-opener.</details>
- *The Blackwell History of the Latin Language*, James Clackson & Geoffrey Horrocks
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>A great single-volume history of Latin, from its origins to its descendants.</details>
- *A Companion to the Latin Language*, James Clackson (ed.)
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Essays on many aspects of Latin. Good to dip into by topic.</details>
- *Beyond Greek: The Beginnings of Latin Literature*, Denis Feeney
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>How Roman literature grew out of Greek models while becoming its own thing.</details>

### Mycenaean Greek

- *The Mycenaean World*, John Chadwick
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>A lively introduction to Mycenaean society, drawn from the Linear B tablets.</details>
- *Linear B: An Introduction*, J. T. Hooker
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>A practical guide to the script and the language behind it.</details>

## Ancient Religion

- *On Greek Religion*, J. Bremmer
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>A concise, insightful overview of how Greek religion actually worked.</details>
- *The Matter of the Gods: Religion and the Roman Empire*, C. Ando
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Makes a strong case for how Roman religion functioned across the Empire.</details>
- *The Gods in Epic: Poets and Critics of the Classical Tradition*, D. Feeney
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Looks at how epic poets handle the gods. Great for literature and religion together.</details>
- *From Jupiter to Christ: On the History of Religion in the Roman Imperial Period*, J. Rüpke
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Traces religious change across the Empire, up to the rise of Christianity.</details>
- *The Gods, the State, and the Individual: Reflections on Civic Religion in Rome*, J. Scheid
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Explains Roman religion as a civic practice rather than personal belief.</details>

## Classical Reception & Popular Culture

- *The Reception of Ancient Virtues and Vices in Modern Popular Culture: Beauty, Bravery, Blood and Glory*, Eran Almagor & Lisa Maurice
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>How ancient ideas of virtue reappear in films, games and TV.</details>
- *Tracking Classical Monsters in Popular Culture*, Liz Gloyn
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>A fun look at how Medusa, the Minotaur and friends live on in modern media.</details>
- *Ancient Greece on British Television*, Fiona Hobden
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Traces how the ancient world has been portrayed on the small screen.</details>
- *Classics for All: Reworking Antiquity in Mass Culture*, Dunstan Lowe & Kim Shahabudin
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Shows how antiquity gets reinvented for wide audiences.</details>
- *Once and Future Antiquities in Science Fiction*, Brett M. Rogers & B. Eldon Stevens
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>Where classics meets sci-fi. A cool and unusual angle.</details>
- *Critical Ancient World Studies: The Case for Forgetting Classics*, Mathura Umachandran & Marchella Ward
  <details><summary>My thoughts</summary>A provocative argument for rethinking how we study the ancient world.</details>
